Ind. Code  ch. 8-1-26  provides  the procedure  for  the Indiana  Utility  Regulatory 
Commission’s Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”) to find violations  of said  chapter. Upon 
review of those findings, the Indiana  Underground Plant Protection  Advisory Committee 
(“Advisory Committee”) reviews those recommendations and recommends civil penalties in the 
Case.   
The Cases received pursuant to Ind. Code ch. 8-1- 26 and ripe for Commiss ion action are 
attached hereto and collectively referred to as the Advisory Committee Recommendations.  
Pursuant to statute, the Advisory Committee has submitted their recommendations  to the 
Commission. The Commission UPHOLDS  the  findings of violations  by the Pipeline  Safety 
Division and APPROVES the recommendations  of the Advisory Committee  as listed  on the 
attached pages. The Assistant General Counsel to  the Division  is directed  to prepare  and send 
notice to the parties advising them of the determination. 
Any approve d civil penalt ies are due withi n 90 da ys of the date of this Order unless 
payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission.   
Any approved trainings must be comple ted no later than 180 days from the date of this 
Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due.   
IT IS SO ORDERED. 
HUSTON, FREEMAN, KREVDA, AND ZIEGNER CONCUR; OBER ABSENT:

input.command:
cd text; cat > $TMPDIR/a.py <<'E'
import re,glob,sys
n=0;t=0;bad=[]
for f in sorted(glob.glob('*.txt')):
    for p in open(f).read().split('=== page')[1:]:
        if 'Respondent:' not in p: continue
        m=re.search(r'civil\s+penalty:?(.*?)Abstentions',p,re.S)
        if not m: bad.append((f,p[:200]));continue
        r=m.group(1)
        d=re.search(r'\$\s*\$?\s*(\d[\d,\s]*)',r)
        amt=0
        if d:
            s=re.sub(r'[,\s]','',d.group(1)) if True else ''
            amt=int(s) if s else 0
        if amt>0:
            n+=1
            if re.search('training',r,re.I): t+=1
        elif '$' in r: bad.append((f,r))
print(n,t,round(100*t/n,1));print(bad)
E
python3 -I $TMPDIR/a.py

cd ../text; sed -i 's/\\\$\\s\*\\\$?\\s\*(\\d\[\\d,\\s\]\*)/\\$\\s*\\$?\\s*(\\d+(?:,\\s?\\d{3})*)/' $TMPDIR/a.py; grep -n "d=re" $TMPDIR/a.py; python3 -I $TMPDIR/a.py; grep -c "Respondent:" *.txt | awk -F: '{s+=$2}END{print s}'

content.text:
Among cases with a headline penalty above $0, **44.7%** have a recommendation containing "training". That is 3,532 of 7,899 cases.

I parsed all 58 order text files. I took the text between "civil penalty" and "Abstentions" as the recommendation. I read the headline penalty as the first "$" amount, ignoring a doubled "$" and any space after a thousands comma. A recommendation like "Training or $5,000 if respondent fails to complete training" counts as $5,000 and contains "training".

The files hold 9,963 cases in total. The other 2,064 have a headline penalty of $0 and are left out. Every recommendation with a "$" sign yielded a parseable amount, so none were dropped.

I didn't check each order's date. I assumed all 58 files fall in 2021–2025, as the question states, and didn't filter by date.
